title: The blind reviewer starts without CLAUDE.md, memory or git snapshot, and the review lock requires it (A34, v0.1)

context.task: Close the v0.1 part of A34: Claude Code puts the project's CLAUDE.md (with AGENTS.md, docs/PLAN.md and .claude/memory/MEMORY.md through its imports) and a git status snapshot with recent commit subjects into every subagent's context before its first tool call, so the blind reviewer is not blind by construction.

select.heading: A34 — La revisión ciega recibe la memoria y las instrucciones del proyecto antes de leer nada

problem: AGENTS 5.1 marks the blind review [enforced]: while the review lock is set, tools/hooks/confine_review_reads.py denies every Read, Grep and Glob outside the package. But Claude Code gives a non-fork subagent, before its first tool call, every CLAUDE.md the main conversation loads (here AGENTS.md, docs/PLAN.md with decisions and measured figures, and the governed memory index) and a git status snapshot with recent commit subjects, which can carry results. Six transcripts of Traianus' blind auditor show CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and the auto-memory index (with prior results) in its context (CASES.md, A34). Claude Code's documentation (read 2026-10-13) gives the switches: `omitClaudeMd: true` in a subagent's definition (v2.1.271 or later) drops the user, project and local CLAUDE.md files; `includeGitInstructions: false` drops the git snapshot for the whole session; a subagent's `memory` field gives it its own memory and turns on Read, Write and Edit.
decisions: D1 Scope, v0.1 (author, 2026-10-13): the reviewer's definition, the git snapshot off in Actuarii, the review lock refused unless both hold, and the skill's text. Out of scope, v0.2: a hook that checks the delegation message, a verdict validated in code, a reviewer run as a separate process. The credentials case is separate.

D2 The reviewer's definition, .claude/agents/blind-reviewer.md, has exactly four frontmatter keys: name (blind-reviewer), description, `tools: Read, Grep, Glob` and `omitClaudeMd: true`. No memory (it would turn on Write and Edit), no skills, no mcpServers, no hooks, no other key: each can add context or tools. Audit rules live in the package (procedure and base documents of the review configuration), never in a memory of the reviewer (author, 2026-10-13).

D3 Its body gains one paragraph, after the bullet about the review package: its context starts, by configuration, without the project's CLAUDE.md files, memory or git snapshot; if its context holds any of them, or the delegation message states an expected or a prior result, it says so in the blindness statement and stops.

D4 .claude/settings.json gains `"includeGitInstructions": false`: no git snapshot for any agent of the session, and no built-in commit and pull request instructions, which Actuarii replaces with its own (docs/PLAN.md, inherited working rules). The ConfigChange hook blocks the change from applying to the running session: expected, it applies to the next one.

D5 `build_review_package.py build --lock` checks, before writing anything, that the review will be blind by configuration: (a) the reviewer's definition exists, its frontmatter parses (the lines between the first `---` line and the next one, each `key: value`; standard library only) and is exactly D2; (b) the effective includeGitInstructions is the JSON boolean false, taken from the first of .claude/settings.local.json, .claude/settings.json and ~/.claude/settings.json that sets the key. A settings file that exists and is not a valid JSON object fails the check. The environment variable CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_GIT_INSTRUCTIONS is not accepted: the agent controls the builder's environment. Managed settings are not read.

D6 When the check fails, the builder writes one stderr line per unmet guarantee, naming the file and the key, writes neither the package nor the lock, and exits 1. Without --lock it behaves as today: a package nobody reviews under the lock confines nothing. unlock is unchanged.
D7 The locations the builder checks are module attributes next to LOCK_PATH, so tests repoint them; never environment variables (the convention of tools/project_config.py).

D8 The blind-review skill (both copies, .claude and .opencode, byte for byte) replaces its `Blind by construction` rule with what holds, by configuration and in code (the confinement of reads, no CLAUDE.md, no memory, no git snapshot, the lock refused otherwise), and what is declared: the delegation message, which the executing agent writes; a managed-policy CLAUDE.md; Claude Code versions before 2.1.271, which ignore omitClaudeMd without an error. It adds a rule: audit rules live in the package; a lesson from a review becomes a governed change to the procedure, approved by the author, never a note of the reviewer. No mention of any project by name (the existing test).
D9 examples/traianus/agents/instrument-auditor.md gains `omitClaudeMd: true`, so the example is not the vulnerable form.

D10 Gates: red-first, each red test seen failing for its stated reason before the change that makes it pass; full-suite, `pytest tests/` exits 0 at the commit; verify-red-green, tools/audit/verify_red_green.py exits 0 on the report.

D11 This contract is launched after A20 and A31 are merged, the last of the three that stay in the v0.1 (author, 2026-10-15); A19 and the option (c) go to the v0.2. Its base commit is stamped at launch. The AGENTS.md wording of 5.1 and the section 9 declarations come in the single AGENTS.md change, not here.

D12 The session's validator requires a Rationale in every proposal (AGENTS.md 2.2). The schema of validate_proposal shown in this session may be an older copy without it: include it anyway, or the proposal comes back INVALID_JSON. .claude/settings.json now also carries the permission perimeter of AGENTS 7.1, pinned by tests/security/test_config_perimeter.py and by PERMISSIONS in tests/security/test_contract_context_hook.py; this contract adds a top-level key and changes nothing in permissions.

D13 tests/security/test_root_off_sys_path.py (A31) runs build_review_package.py as a program and checks that its header carries the sys.path pattern exactly once: keep that pattern and its place as they are, and put any new import of the standard library after it. If that test fails, stop and report; it is not in files_may_touch.

behaviours.statement: .claude/agents/blind-reviewer.md has exactly the D2 frontmatter and the D3 paragraph; the rest of its body is unchanged.
.claude/settings.json sets includeGitInstructions to false; its other keys and values are unchanged.

`build --lock` refuses as D6 says when the reviewer's definition is missing, does not parse, lacks omitClaudeMd: true, has any key beyond D2's (memory, skills, mcpServers, hooks, …), or has other tools; and when the effective includeGitInstructions is not false (unset everywhere, true at the winning level, or a local true over a project false), or a settings file it reads is not a valid JSON object.
With a compliant reviewer and an effective false (also a project false over a user true), `build --lock` writes the package and the lock exactly as today.
The blind-review skill carries the D8 text, identical in .claude and .opencode.

tests.must_catch: a reviewer definition without omitClaudeMd: true, with a memory, skills or any key beyond D2's, with other tools, or without the D3 paragraph
tests.reason: today the definition has no omitClaudeMd and no such paragraph

tests.must_catch: settings without includeGitInstructions false, or with another set of top-level keys
tests.reason: today the key is absent and the pinned set of top-level keys does not include it

tests.must_catch: a review lock set although the reviewer would receive CLAUDE.md, a memory, other tools or a git snapshot, or a refusal that writes a package or a lock, or a check that trusts the environment variable
tests.reason: today build --lock checks nothing about the reviewer or the settings

tests.must_catch: a change to a compliant build --lock, to build without --lock, or to unlock
tests.reason: these behave as B4 and B5 at the base commit, given a compliant reviewer and settings in the fixture

tests.must_catch: a blind-review skill that still claims blindness by construction without naming what is declared, or copies that differ
tests.reason: today the skill's rule claims blindness by construction and names no declared channel

commit_message: fix(revisión ciega): el revisor sin CLAUDE.md, memoria ni git, y el candado lo exige (A34)
